label: Schaffer on the functional-organ example and its limited evidential force
locator: §2.1, p.47 and note 24, with the assessment on p.50
interpretation: Schaffer contrasts aggregates with integrated wholes and cites functional definition/integration for an organism-organ example of whole-first priority, explicitly qualifying its Aristotelian attribution. He uses it within a common-sense rationale and on p.50 treats the resulting intuitive case as at most a weak default rather than empirical establishment. This records a reasoned candidate for an intermediate D-edge in the paper’s dependence discussion, not a source proof that organ function determines the numerical identity or existential dependence of an actual material object. It specifies no immediate/full ground or independently sufficient productive power, and does not license every proper-part edge. Aristotle’s underlying text has not been directly read in this slice.
attribution: The passage states that the organism-organ case supports the common-sense priority of integrated wholes, while giving the common-sense argument at most default force, which is the premise.
